newsitem.title: INDIA: Japan's Nitsuko in talks for India tie-up.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Nitsuko in talks for India tie-up.

text.p: Japan's Nitsuko Corp is in talks with India's Enkay Telecommunications to set up a plant to manufacture key telephone systems in India, a company official said on Tuesday.
"We are in discussions with Enkay to set up a manufacturing plant in India," Akira Miyazawa, a senior vice-president of Nitsuko, told Reuters. The deal would be finalised in a few months, he added.
His comments came after he spoke at a function in Bombay to launch a new range of key telephone systems and telecom equipment.

"We have a network of 12 offices all over India, so Nitsuko would not have to make a large investment," said Nanik Rupani, chairman of Enkay, told Reuters. "It will probably be about 300 million to 400 million rupees, phased over a period of several years."
He gave no further details about the plant.

Rupani said Enkay's turnover in key telephone systems in the financial year 1995/96 (April-March) was 650 million rupees. He estimated the size of the market at around 900 million to one billion rupees.
"This figure is increasing at the rate of about 20 percent each year," he added.
He said statistics showed India has a telephone density of about one instrument for every 100 people, with about 12 million instruments nationwide.
Nitsuko has been associated with Enkay since 1984, when it marketed key telephone systems manufactured by a state-run firm under a technical tie-up with Nitsuko.

Subsequently, Nitsuko has collaborated directly with Enkay to introduce key telephone systems in India, Enkay said in a statement. It said it commands over 70 percent of the market, with more than 15,000 customers.
